Definition: from the same as G2945; to encircle, i.e. surround:--compass (about), come (stand) round about.
BiblicalUsage: To compass about is to surround, and it happens to Paul, to Jericho, to Jesus, and to Jerusalem. In Acts 14:20 the disciples stood round about Paul after he was stoned, and he rose up; in Hebrews 11:30 the walls of Jericho fell after they were compassed about seven days; in John 10:24 the Jews came round about Jesus demanding a plain answer; and in Luke 21:20 Jerusalem compassed with armies is the sign its desolation is near.
TheologicalSignificance: My position is that the word's four scenes are the whole story of surrounding: the church gathers round the fallen, faith circles the walls until they fall, and enemies circle the city until it falls. Enemies circle, the church gathers, and God decides which circle holds.
